Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & retention requirements (FinPay)

Hi Sanjay / Leah —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery: 

- Goal: Integrate Redwood Hosted API for payment routing & enriched risk signals.
- Main constraint: FinPay legal flagged a strict data-retention requirement for payment PII (they prefer 0-retention of payloads).
- Other asks: data residency in us-east, SOC 2 evidence, and ability to redact payloads before storage.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll share a short proposed retention compromise (what we can do in Hosted) for your internal review.
2) Rafael will outline the technical flow for redaction/metadata-only logging.
3) If acceptable, we can route this to legal for a scoped retention exception.

Attached: FinPay_MVP_requirements.pdf (brief)

Would it help if we proposed a 30-day ephemeral logs approach limited to hashed identifiers + request metadata for troubleshooting, with clear controls? Open to other ideas — putting Rafael / Marissa on copy to iterate.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finpay.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & retention requirements (FinPay)

Camila — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Our legal team is pushing for 0-retention of payment payloads that contain PANs, CVV, and unmasked account numbers.
- We understand debugging needs, but any logs that could reconstruct PANs are a hard no.
- We're open to metadata-only logging (timestamps, request-id, error codes) and hashed/peppered user identifiers for correlation.

I’m attaching our data classification matrix so you can see exactly which fields are considered sensitive. Can you and Rafael propose a specific dataflow showing where we would redact or hash fields, and what would be retained for 30 days (if anything)?

If we can get a concrete proposal, I’ll run it by legal and security to see whether they will approve a scoped exception.

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Patel | Head of Integrations, FinPay
sanjay.patel@finpay.com

Attachment: data_classification_matrix.xlsx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finpay.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & retention requirements (FinPay)

Thanks Sanjay — looping in a concise technical proposal below.

Proposal (short):
- Payload handling: Redwood will accept the full request over TLS, then apply customer-configured redaction rules in the ingestion pipeline. For FinPay, rule set = remove PAN/CVV fields + mask account numbers to last4.
- Retention model: 0-retention for raw payloads (we do not persist full payloads).
- Ephemeral troubleshooting logs: retain service-level metadata for 30 days: timestamp, request-id, route, model-version, response-status, error-trace (no message text), and a hashed user_id (SHA-256 with customer-specific salt stored in KMS).
- Access and controls: logs encrypted at rest (AES-256), KMS-managed keys per-customer, strict RBAC (only SRE on-call with justification), full audit trail for access.
- Rollback / purge: automatic 30-day TTL enforced by storage layer; immediate admin purge API for emergency erasure.

If this looks good we can formalize in an exception letter for legal. We can also provide a sequence diagram and sample redaction rules in the next email.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finpay.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & retention requirements (FinPay)

Hi all — Neha from Redwood Legal. Thanks for the clear proposal, Rafael. High level this is workable, but legal will need the following to draft a scoped retention exception: 

1) Exact list of fields that will be redacted vs hashed (please paste names/JSON paths).
2) Confirmation that hashing uses per-customer salt via KMS and that salts are never exported.
3) Details on who (roles) can access ephemeral logs and the approval workflow.
4) A sample purge/rollback runbook and confirmation of TTL enforcement (immutable once set except via admin purge).

If those items are satisfactory we’ll prepare a limited "Data Retention Exception" (DPA exhibit) that:
- Grants 30-day metadata retention for troubleshooting only
- Requires per-request redaction for specified PII
- Includes audit and notification obligations

I’ve attached our standard retention_exception_template.docx — I can draft the first pass of the exception for your review. Once you sign, we’ll provide a DocuSign envelope for execution.

Neha Kapoor | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 18:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & retention requirements (FinPay)

Neha / Camila — this looks very reasonable.

We’ll pull the exact JSON paths (developer team will respond by Friday) and confirm the list of fields to be redacted. From a timeline perspective:
- Please draft the exception and share by Friday EOD if possible.
- We’ll review with FinPay legal early next week.
- If approved, we’ll sign via DocuSign; please include the RACI and a rollback procedure in the doc.

One more ask: include a short paragraph in the exception that clarifies the rollback/purge API and the SLA for emergency purge (we need <24h).

Thanks — Sanjay
